content.overview: Cannabis/hemp germination responds to temperature, water availability, oxygen, seed condition and protocol design. Research values are evidence, not automatic facility recipes.

sections.title: Temperature changes both rate and success
sections.body: Controlled hemp studies show a broad favorable range rather than one universal optimum, and responses differed across reports and cultivars. High-temperature exposure can move from inhibition to loss of viability with duration.

sections.title: Treatment effects need context
sections.body: A cannabis protocol reported rapid germination using hydrogen peroxide under controlled conditions, including old seed. That demonstrates a tested method, not a requirement for all lots or facilities.

sections.title: Change one interpretable factor at a time
sections.body: When troubleshooting, preserve treatment identity, timing and control/comparison conditions so a later outcome can be tied to evidence rather than memory or multiple simultaneous changes.

commonMistakes: Treating a research protocol value as a universal production target.
Reporting successful seedlings without preserving the original denominator.
Changing multiple variables at once and then claiming one caused the result.
content.practicalApplication: Given three germination protocols from different studies, identify which parameters can be treated as evidence, which remain cultivar/facility-specific, and what a controlled comparison would need.
content.summary: Use source-controlled evidence, preserve identity and denominators, and keep observations separate from explanations.
